- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.67) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >30% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 2–3 standard deviations above recent mean.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to forecast slope.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon; if forecast deviates >1.5σ from recent 7-day average, adjust toward mean.  
- Forecasts with sentiment history dominated by 0.00 (neutral) show high variance; use 3-day rolling average to smooth and anchor forecast.
